lines.text: Do you know how an AI data center keeps from melting?
Every time you ask an AI something, a chip somewhere gets hot. Really hot.
One modern AI rack can pull about a hundred and twenty kilowatts. That's roughly a hundred homes, in one cabinet.
Old server rooms just blew cold air down the aisles. At this heat, fans alone can't keep up.
So engineers bolt a metal cold plate right onto each chip, with liquid running through tiny channels inside.
The liquid soaks up the heat, carries it out of the rack, and hands it to a second loop of water.
Up on the roof, that warm water dumps its heat into the air, comes back cold, and round it goes.
Orbi Transfer keeps its server cool another way. It never carries your file. It just signs a ticket, and the bytes fly straight to storage.
